## Goal

Validate the complete Docker GPU-option grammar before deriving NVIDIA launch intent. Related: [#1895](https://github.com/RobTand/prismabuild/issues/1895)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unknown or duplicate keys, invalid counts and malformed CSV produce no intent
- [ ] accepted quoted device and driver forms preserve their meaning
- [ ] Feed unknown/duplicate keys, invalid counts, and malformed quoted CSV to the parser; pre-fix code records intent from the recognized subset, while repaired parsing refuses with no intent.

## Likely files

- `tools/fleet/docker`
- `tests/test_docker_shim_gpu_options.py`

## Context

Source issue: https://github.com/RobTand/prismabuild/issues/1968

https://github.com/RobTand/prismabuild/issues/1895

Related: https://github.com/RobTand/prismabuild/issues/1895

<details><summary>Original text</summary>

Follow-up to #1895 (the GPU container-runtime fence), from its round-6 review. Non-blocking.

## Finding

`tools/fleet/docker` (~line 480) builds NVIDIA intent from a `--gpus` value by extracting `driver=` and `device=`. It ignores the other fields, even invalid ones. These inputs still report NVIDIA intent:
- `driver=cdi,device=nvidia.com/gpu=all,count=bogus`
- unknown keys
- duplicate counts
- a bare quote inside an unquoted device field
- an unquoted multi-device list

The round-6 reviewer reproduced each one. Docker's own parser (docker/cli `opts/gpus.go`) rejects these before it creates a container, so no daemon events follow and no fence can result. This is a fail-closed helper gap, not an operational false fence.

## Required

- Validate the complete `--gpus` grammar the same way docker/cli does before constructing intent: keys, duplicate keys, counts, and CSV quoting.
- Return no intent for anything docker/cli would reject.
- Tests for each malformed form above, and for the valid forms #1895 already accepts.


</details>
title: [P3] Reject malformed GPU options before recording container intent
